# QuotaBird

> Quick reality checks for people who carry a number: thirteen free, one-minute tools for sellers and sales managers (deals, pipeline, quota, territories, partners, reps, reviews), plus short field notes. Everything runs in the browser; nothing is stored. Built by Mark Flournoy, who led partner sales teams at AWS.

The tools are plain web pages. Each asks five questions (yes / sort of / no) or takes a few numbers, then gives a verdict, the question a manager will ask, and one thing to do first. Shared results are encoded in the URL fragment; no accounts, no uploads, no AI.

## Your deal

- [Deal Check](https://quotabird.com/deal/): Five questions (customer, money, power, path, now) that separate proof from hopium in a federal deal. (before you put it in commit.)
- [Account Check](https://quotabird.com/account/): Five questions that tell you whether you know the account or only the opportunity in front of you: mission, money, power, incumbents, how they buy. One minute, nothing stored. (when you only know one person there.)
- [Competition Check](https://quotabird.com/competition/): Five questions that tell you whether the incumbent, the competitor, or doing nothing is beating you right now. One minute, nothing stored. (when you are not sure you are ahead.)

## Your number

- [Quota Check](https://quotabird.com/quota/): Your quota against your on-target earnings, judged by what the number is measured in: new bookings, cloud consumption growth, or a whole book. Free, in your browser, nothing stored. (the day the number lands.)
- [Territory Check](https://quotabird.com/territory/): Can the patch make the number, or are you being asked to grow where nobody could? Five questions for sellers. Nothing stored. (month one in a new patch.)
- [Discount Check](https://quotabird.com/discount/): They want a discount. See what it costs in your commission and the company's margin before you say yes. Free, in your browser, nothing stored. (when they ask you to sharpen the pencil.)
- [Commission Check](https://quotabird.com/commission/): Deal size and commission rate in, what you actually take home out, after the share you set aside for taxes. Free, in your browser, nothing stored. (when it closes.)

## Your team

- [Pipeline Check](https://quotabird.com/): Target, pipeline and win rate in, the gap out. 3X is a rule of thumb; your win rate says what you actually need. (quarterly, before the review.)
- [Risk Check](https://quotabird.com/risk/): Coverage says whether you have enough pipeline. This says how fragile it is: concentration, aging, next steps, timing and creation. Five questions, one minute, nothing stored. (when coverage looks fine and you do not trust it.)
- [Rep Check](https://quotabird.com/rep/): Is it the rep, the patch, a skill gap or an effort gap? Five questions for sales managers. No names, nothing stored. (when a rep is worrying you.)
- [Partner Check](https://quotabird.com/partner/): Five questions that separate a partner who sells with you from a logo on a slide. For partner managers. One minute, nothing stored. (before you renew the partnership.)
- [OLR Check](https://quotabird.com/olr/): Five questions that test the case you're making for a rep in OLR, then the room grills you. No names, no ratings, nothing stored. (review season.)

## Any meeting

- [Brief Check](https://quotabird.com/brief/): Five questions about the doc, deck or QBR you're about to present, then the room grills you. Nothing uploaded, nothing stored. (when someone in the room can say no.)

## Free printable

- [The Sales Manager's Field Kit](https://quotabird.com/kit/): a free, printable field kit for sales managers: inheriting a team, one-on-ones, the forecast call, pipeline, managing up, a struggling rep, review season, when to leave a rep alone, and six worksheets.

## Sales Math Library

- [How much pipeline do you actually need?](https://quotabird.com/math/pipeline-coverage/): Required pipeline coverage is 1 ÷ your qualified win rate. A 3X coverage ratio assumes a 33% win rate; at 20% you need 5X, at 25% you need 4X.
- [What your quota-to-OTE ratio really says](https://quotabird.com/math/quota-to-ote/): Quota ÷ OTE equals your variable share of OTE divided by your commission rate at 100% attainment. SaaS new-bookings plans cluster around 4×; cloud consumption plans, paid at a fraction of a percent, run far higher by design.
- [What a discount really costs you and the company](https://quotabird.com/math/discount-math/): A discount cuts your commission by exactly the discount percentage, and cuts gross margin to 1 − (1 − margin) ÷ (1 − discount). A 15% discount on a 40% margin leaves about 29%, not 25%.
- [Why your commission check is smaller than the math](https://quotabird.com/math/commission-take-home/): US employers may withhold federal income tax on separately paid commissions at a flat 22% (37% on supplemental wages above $1 million in a year), plus 7.65% Social Security and Medicare, before any state tax. That is withholding, not the tax you finally owe.

## Field Notes

- [3X is a win rate in disguise](https://quotabird.com/notes/3x-is-a-win-rate/): Everybody plans to it. Almost nobody asks where it came from.
- [Why I don't start with BANT or MEDDIC](https://quotabird.com/notes/why-not-bant-or-meddic/): They're useful when you're working a deal. The trouble is the moment before that.
- [If three people failed in the same patch](https://quotabird.com/notes/three-people-same-patch/): You probably don't have three bad reps.
- [Your quota went up 30%. Did your territory?](https://quotabird.com/notes/quota-went-up-did-your-territory/): The number moved. Ask what else did.
- [They asked for 15% off. What are you buying with it?](https://quotabird.com/notes/fifteen-percent-off/): A discount is a purchase. Make sure you get something for it.
- [Your best rep hates internal meetings. Is that a problem?](https://quotabird.com/notes/best-rep-hates-meetings/): Probably not the one you think.
